methodology: Read Qur'an 11:56–60 in Arabic with published English translations (E-Quran, Quran.GG); screened verse-specific earlier textual parallels conservatively. No earlier primary-text passage was independently verified this session. Shared generic judgment/prophet motifs are not sufficient to assign source associations. Do not infer literary dependence or identify Ad with a Biblical people.

research_dossier.title: Hūd and ʿĀd: trust, warning, rescue and judgment (11:56–60)
research_dossier.narrative: Hūd declares trust in the Lord of all creatures (11:56), warns that rejecting his delivered message will not harm God (11:57), and the account concludes with the rescue of Hūd and his believers (11:58), ʿĀd's rejection (11:59), and a curse in this life and at resurrection (11:60).
research_dossier.comparative_scope: Assess independently datable ancient Arabian epigraphy and pre-Islamic literary traditions for ʿĀd/Hūd, plus precisely located older prophetic warning and collective rescue motifs. Do not treat shared motifs as direct narrative witnesses.
research_dossier.chronology_and_witness_caveat: No dated pre-Islamic textual witness naming Hūd or recounting this specific episode was authenticated in this batch. Composition, redaction, manuscript witness and modern translation dates must be separately established before any relationship becomes public.
research_dossier.similarities_and_differences: No independently checked earlier text; therefore no specific similarities or differences are asserted as established comparisons.
research_dossier.scholarly_interpretation: No scholarly dependence hypothesis is endorsed; unresolved comparisons require explicit attribution and primary-text verification.
research_dossier.bibliography_status: Qur'anic Arabic and English text inspected; no independently verified pre-Islamic comparative bibliography yet.
